sections.h2: Where is the Bertie County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office sits on the first floor of the Bertie County courthouse at the corner of King and Dundee streets in Windsor. The physical address is 108 Dundee Street, Windsor, NC 27983, and the mailing address is PO Box 340 at the same ZIP code.

The county lists office hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but recording hours run only from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. daily, so a deed that arrives at 4:45 waits until the next morning. The phone number is (252) 794-5309 and the fax is (252) 794-5374. Holidays and bad weather can close the office.

The office now accepts electronic real estate recordings, which closing attorneys often use instead of carrying paper to Windsor. Visitors can stop by during office hours.

sections.h2: What does the Bertie County Register of Deeds record and keep?
sections.html:
The register is the custodian of deeds, deeds of trust, powers of attorney, assumed names, plats, maps and military discharge records for the county. North Carolina voters elect the register every two years, and the office works under Chapter 161 of the General Statutes.

Recording is what protects a buyer. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance, option, lease of more than three years or right of first refusal does not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the order of registration by time. A signed deed that sits in a drawer gives the buyer very little protection.

  • Real estate records can be searched online from 1977 forward, or by book number starting at Book 600.
  • The earliest land and grant transactions on file go back to 1722.
  • Records are indexed by name only, so the office cannot tell you who owns a street address.
  • For an owner lookup by address, call the county tax assessor's mapping line at (252) 794-5311.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Bertie County?
sections.html:
Recording fees are the same in every North Carolina county. A standard instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each additional page, and a deed of trust or mortgage costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 for each page after that.

Bertie County Register of Deeds uniform fee schedule under G.S. 161-10 (county fee page)
ItemFee
Instrument other than a deed of trust or mortgage$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page
Extra instrument in the same document$10.00
Non-standard document$25.00 plus the recording fee

Plat$21.00 per sheet

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Call the office at (252) 794-5309 if a document has unusual page counts or multiple instruments.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Bertie County deed?
sections.html:
The state excise tax is $1.00 on each $500, or fraction of $500, of the price or value conveyed. The seller, whom the statute calls the transferor, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, normally out of closing proceeds.

The tax is split on receipt: half stays in the county general fund and half goes to the Department of Revenue each month, less refunds and the county's allowance. A parcel that lies in two counties is taxed in the county that holds the greater value. Ask the closing attorney for the exact figure from the sale price on the settlement statement, because the rounding rule for each $500 matters.

sections.h2: What recording rules apply only in Bertie County?
sections.html:
Bertie County has used a recording resolution since June 1, 1991, under G.S. 161-30. The register may not accept any map or instrument affecting real property unless the name and address of the person to receive it back is on its face, and the grantee's permanent mailing address is also on its face.

The statewide document standards also apply, and the office prints them for filers. Pages must be 8-1/2 by 11 or 8-1/2 by 14, with a 3 inch blank margin at the top of the first page and a half inch margin on the other sides, black type on white paper, text of at least 9 points on one side only, and the type of instrument shown at the top below the margin. A document that misses a standard is still recorded after a $25.00 non-standard fee, although the register may waive that fee for a slightly small font when the text is legible.

A short checklist before you send a deed to Windsor:

  • Return address and grantee mailing address on the first page
  • Deed signed and notarized
  • Margin and font standards met
  • Recording fee and excise tax ready to pay

sections.h2: How do you change names on a Bertie County deed?
sections.html:
You prepare a new deed. The register's FAQ says a new deed must be drafted by an attorney, signed and notarized, then presented for recording with the fee.

The same rule covers a sale, a gift and a transfer after a death. A contract for deed, also called a land contract, has its own recording step in Chapter 47H: the seller must record the contract or a memorandum of it within five business days. Where a seller keeps title under such a contract, a buyer can cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing.

If a lender has been paid off, ask for a satisfaction of the deed of trust and have it recorded. The county does not charge for recording satisfactions, and a clean record keeps a sale from stalling at the title check.

sections.h2: How does the register of deeds fit into a Bertie County sale?
sections.html:
The closing attorney or title agent searches the register's records, records the new deed and any new deed of trust, and pays the excise tax out of the settlement. A seller does not file anything personally in most sales. Census QuickFacts counts 9,116 housing units in Bertie County for July 2025, and every deed for those parcels, from a small Windsor lot to a rural farm tract, is recorded in the single courthouse office on Dundee Street.

Unpaid property taxes are the one record problem that surfaces outside the register's office. They are a lien on the parcel and must be cleared with the tax collector; see our Bertie County property tax guide for due dates, relief programs and appeals. Title problems from older instruments, such as an unreleased deed of trust or an estate that was never opened, are fixed by recording the missing paper before closing, and the register's long records back to 1722 help trace them.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Bertie County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office phone is (252) 794-5309 and the fax is (252) 794-5374. Staff take questions about recording requirements and fees without an appointment.

faqs.q: How much does the Bertie County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: A standard deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for each added page. A deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages. A non-standard document adds $25.00, and satisfactions carry no fee.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed transfer tax in Bertie County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. The state excise tax is $1.00 per $500 of value, paid to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can the Bertie County Register of Deeds tell me who owns a property?
faqs.a: Not by street address. The register's index is by name only, so call the county tax assessor's mapping office at (252) 794-5311 to find an owner from an address.

faqs.q: How far back do Bertie County land records go?
faqs.a: Land and grant transactions on file start in 1722. Online real estate searches cover 1977 to the present, or Book 600 onward by book number.
